text:
maya.s: heads up — customer (BrightCart) reporting repeated 429s and large latency spikes on their dedicated pool since 03:40 UTC. appears tied to autoscaler bouncing.
jordan: saw that alert. metrics look like sharp queue spikes then immediate scale-up, then scale-down before KV cache warms, repeat loop. noisy neighbor maybe? :thinking_face:
leo: got logs from scale-controller for tenant brightcart-01 — attaching snippet:
```
2026-03-17T03:39:58Z INFO scale-controller: eval=queue_len=820, cpu=12%, gpu=45% -> scale_up to 6
2026-03-17T03:40:12Z INFO scale-controller: eval=queue_len=10, cpu=8% -> scale_down to 2
2026-03-17T03:40:45Z WARN router: request=brightcart-01 req_id=ac3f throttle=429 reason=token_bucket_exhausted
```
maya.s: interesting — queue_len spikes for short bursts then collapses. autoscaler cooldown currently 30s, smoothing window 60s.
jordan: that cooldown is too low for workloads with cold KV/cache effects. scale down happening before prefixes warm -> user requests hit uncached slow path -> queue spikes again.
aleks: customer says they have periodic batch inference jobs that flood the pool every ~5m for 30s. that matches the sawtooth pattern. noisy neighbor indeed.
leo: repro steps I used from our side (dev cluster) to emulate:

1) run 4 workers pinned to pool `dedicated-brightcart`
2) run a short load burst script:

```
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST" -d '{"model":"open-7b","input":"warm me"}' &
done
```

observed same scale up -> immediate scale down -> repeat.
maya.s: put a quick mitigation plan in the ticket: increase cooldown to 180s and smoothing window to 180s for that pool; set min_replicas=4; enable short-term tenant-level burst cap to protect others. Also request customer to stagger their batch jobs.
jordan: LGTM for experiment. we should add a prefill/warm RPC on scale up too — trigger 1 warm request per new replica to prime KV cache before routing live traffic.
leo: implemented change on staging cluster: `cooldown=180s, smoothing=180s, min_replicas=4, burst_cap=250rps` — running test for 30m and will compare p95 latency and 429 count.
sre-bot: automated check: applying config change to pool dedicated-brightcart in staging. rollout id: r-20260317-001. ci:passed.
aleks: also found billing noise: customer noticed a jump in token billing during the flaps — they believe double-processing happened. can we confirm dedup or retry path causing duplicate charges?
maya.s: initial look: requests that hit 429 from router are not charged, but retries that succeeded later may be. if clients retry aggressively, they can incur additional cost. we should recommend client retry policy change and enable `retry-after` header on 429s.
jordan: adding a short term helpdesk template for BrightCart: explain root cause (bursty batch -> autoscale oscillation -> cache cold path -> repeated 429s). recommend config changes + stagger + client backoff. cc @sales to handle billing empathy.
leo: staging results after 25m: p95 dropped from 1.8s -> 420ms, 429s reduced from ~120/min -> 6/min. scale churn rate decreased 4x. looks promising.
maya.s: great. plan for prod rollout at 10:00 UTC after a one-hour readout. schedule: change pool config, monitor for 2 hours, revert if we see >5x baseline error increase.
aleks: filed support ticket #SUP-2026-1987 and flagged for billing review.
jordan: follow-ups: (1) implement warm-prefill RPC on scale up task (issue #INF-7123), (2) consider tenant-level burst shaping in router (INF-7124), (3) telemetry: emit `scale_event_reason` in traces so we can auto-detect these sawtooth patterns.
leo: copying short curl to reproduce for eng playbook:

```
seq 1 500 | xargs -n1 -P50 -I{} curl -s -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TEST" -d '{"model":"open-7b","input":"prefill test"}'
```
maya.s: ok assigning: leo -> run prod rollout and watch, jordan -> coordinate with sales/support on customer comms, aleks -> billing follow-up. ping me if any deviation. :thumbsup:
jordan: noted. will prepare customer note and link escalation for billing.
leo: prod change applied at 10:07 UTC, monitoring dashboards show initial stability. will post results in 2h.
aleks: billing team acknowledged ticket and will respond within SLA window.
maya.s: closing loop — please add short postmortem if prod change continues > 24h. thanks team.
